value.rationale: Finite-state inhibitory oscillator synchronization is a classical nonlinear dynamical question; exact attraction-basin sizes and periods are natural invariants on the canonical dense bipartite family. The theorem exposes a structurally meaningful dichotomy: asynchronous period-three/four cycles have no transient basin; every other state globally synchronizes by a sharp six-step cutoff. The full exact two-parameter layer census and balanced-shore exponential nonsynchronization law are nontrivial quantitative refinements of previously qualitative tree-network criteria. Four-cycles appear only in the thick-biclique graph family, beyond the excluded star boundary; the statement is neither a small finite table nor a generic relabelling of an earlier count.
